thread:
jasmin: Customer on PRO account reports batch rerank returns wrong candidate pairing when input has sparse per-query lists. They say top-k looks shifted across queries.
alex: Can you paste the request_id + a minimal repro payload? Also which model/route?
jasmin: request_id: rq_0a9f3c2b, route: /v1/rerank, model: rerank-small-v1. Repro payload below (sanitized):
```json
{
  "queries": ["q1", "q2", "q3"],
  "candidates": [
    ["a1", "a2"],
    [],
    ["b1"]
  ]
}
```
Result mapping from the SDK shows q2 results contain a1,a2 (shifted left) instead of empty array.
sean: Oof. Is the client sending anything like content-length mismatch or gzip chunking? Any proxies in front?
jasmin: Customer is using our python SDK 0.14. They send gzip on large payloads but this test was small and uncompressed. No proxy.
maria: Can you paste the raw server-side parsed request we logged? I can check indices.
jasmin: Server parsed JSON (from our request-log):
```json
{
  "queries": ["q1", "q2", "q3"],
  "candidates_flat": ["a1", "a2", "b1"],
  "per_query_counts": [2,0,1]
}
```
alex: Hmm parsed looks fine. The issue may be in our unpack routine that splits flat candidates by counts. If counts are correct, it should be fine. Can you share the exact splitting code and any recent commits in batch-unpack? @sean fyi.
sean: I pulled a recent change to batch-unpack (PR#482) — it added a micro-optimization that used an iterator and mutated an index in place. Will run local unit tests for sparse cases.
maria: Customer also reported intermittent occurrence — sometimes correct, sometimes shifted. That suggests a race or mutation bug, not upstream formatting.
jasmin: Repro steps I gave to customer: 1) use SDK v0.14, 2) send queries/candidates exactly as above, 3) call /v1/rerank with batch=true 4) check mapping. They reproduced locally and attached screenshots.
alex: Good. Can we add targeted unit tests for cases with empty per-query candidate lists and run on CI? If fails, create hotfix branch.
sean: I ran unit tests locally, saw failure when using iterator approach. Quick patch: switch back to simple index arithmetic and avoid mutating shared state. Patch applied to branch fix/batch-unpack-sparse.
jasmin: I deployed a canary to the staging cluster and re-ran the customer's payload — mapping now correct. Customer asked for timeline for prod fix and wants explanation.
maria: Prepare a short post-mortem and include repro steps, root cause (iterator mutating index -> mis-split flat candidate array when per_query_counts includes zeros), and mitigation (unit tests + revert optimization + add structured request validation). Also recommend SDK update note to ensure clients send explicit per_query_counts or nested arrays.
alex: @support-bot please open incident ticket INC-3498, tag: rerank, severity: medium, assignee: eng-ml.
support-bot: Created INC-3498 — "misaligned candidates for sparse per-query lists". Link: https://redwood.example.com/incidents/INC-3498 :white_check_mark:
jasmin: I'll reply to customer with rollback timeline and offer a temporary workaround: expand empty candidate lists to explicit [] in SDK so server splits reliably. Customer OK with workaround and asked for ETA next week for prod patch.
sean: I'll ship the patch tomorrow morning GMT and coordinate rollout.
maria: Thanks team. I'll draft the post-mortem and add automated regression tests to the rerank test matrix. :thumbsup:
